identity.title: [Specific treatment of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy: established disease-modifying agents and emerging mechanisms].

content.abstract: Transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), in which fibrillary protein deposits accumulate in the cardiac extracellular space, has changed within a few years from a rare condition regarded as therapeutically futile into a causally treatable and increasingly recognised cause of heart failure. Every specific therapy requires a secure diagnosis, with prior exclusion of alternative causes such as light-chain (AL) amyloidosis. Two mechanistic principles are central to the approved treatment options: stabilisation of the transthyretin (TTR) tetramer (Vyndaqel(R), Beyonttra(R)) and reduction of hepatic production through TTR gene silencing (Amvuttra(R)). For the stabilisers and the siRNA agent vutrisiran, randomised trials demonstrate a reduction in all-cause mortality and cardiovascular events; the survival benefit typically becomes apparent months after commencing treatment thus, arguing for the earliest possible initiation of treatment. Two further promising approaches are currently under investigation in phase III trials: antibody-mediated depletion of already deposited amyloid (so-called <<depleters>>) and one-time gene editing (using CRISPR-Cas9). Both offer, for the first time, the prospect of a meaningful regression of amyloid burden and thus of a degree of regression in disease stage. This article classifies the approved agents by mechanism in a practice-oriented manner, discusses the selection, sequencing and combination of therapies as well as the monitoring of treatment response, and provides an outlook on agents in development.
